intro: SQL database se baat karne ki language hai, aur Python ka sqlite3 module bina server ke wahi SQL chalane deta hai. Is section me table banana, CRUD, WHERE/ORDER BY, aggregate, JOIN aur parameterized queries practice hote hain.
theory: Relational table rows aur columns me data rakhti hai; primary key row ko uniquely identify karti hai aur foreign key doosri table se link banati hai.
SELECT columns FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY column LIMIT n — SQL ka reading order isi tarah likha jata hai, execution order thoda alag hota hai.
Aggregate functions COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX group ke upar kaam karte hain; GROUP BY ke saath non-aggregated columns group key me hone chahiye.
JOIN do tables ko key par jodta hai: INNER sirf matches, LEFT saare left rows plus matches. JOIN ke baad duplicate keys row count badha sakti hain.
Parameterized query (`?` placeholder + tuple) SQL injection rokta hai aur values ko safely quote karta hai. String concatenation kabhi nahi.
syntax:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT)")
conn.execute("INSERT INTO users (name, city) VALUES (?, ?)", ("Asha", "pune"))
conn.commit()

SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS users, AVG(score) AS avg_score
FROM users
GROUP BY city
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY avg_score DESC;

examples.code:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER, name TEXT)')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE orders (user_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER)')
conn.executemany('INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?)', [(1, 'Asha'), (2, 'Ravi')])
conn.executemany('INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?)', [(1, 100), (1, 50)])
print(conn.execute('SELECT users.name, SUM(orders.amount) FROM users JOIN orders ON users.id = orders.user_id GROUP BY users.name').fetchall())
explain: JOIN users aur orders ko key par jodta hai, phir GROUP BY total deta hai.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye SQL + Databases ka basic building block hai.

examples.code:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript('''
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER);
INSERT INTO customers (name) VALUES ('Asha'), ('Ravi');
INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, amount) VALUES (1, 100), (1, 50);
''')
rows = conn.execute('''
SELECT customers.name, COALESCE(SUM(orders.amount), 0) AS total
FROM customers
LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id
GROUP BY customers.id
ORDER BY total DESC
''').fetchall()
print(rows)
explain: LEFT JOIN + COALESCE se un customers ka 0 total bhi aata hai jinke koi order nahi.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Application ka data users/orders/payments tables me hota hai; reports JOIN + GROUP BY se banti hain.
Analytics me "per city per day" numbers GROUP BY se aate hain, aur filters WHERE me lagte hain — dono ko mix karna common bug hai.
Har write query parameterized honi chahiye; user input ko SQL string me jodna injection ka sabse bada source hai.

interview.q: WHERE aur HAVING me fark batao.
interview.a: WHERE individual rows ko filter karta hai GROUP BY se pehle; HAVING groups ko filter karta hai aggregate ke baad. Aggregate condition HAVING me likhi jati hai.

interview.q: INNER JOIN aur LEFT JOIN me kya chunenge?
interview.a: INNER sirf matching rows deta hai; LEFT left table ki saari rows deta hai aur match na hone par NULL. "Kaun missing hai" dhoondhne ke liye LEFT + IS NULL use hota hai.

interview.q: SQL injection kaise rokete hain?
interview.a: Parameterized queries se — `?` placeholder aur values tuple/list me. String concatenation se user input SQL ban jata hai, jo injection ka source hai.

interview.q: Index kya karta hai aur kab nuksan deta hai?
interview.a: Index lookup ko fast karta hai (B-tree), par har write par maintain hota hai aur disk leta hai. WHERE/JOIN columns par index; bahut zyada indexes write slow kar dete hain.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye SQL + Databases ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.

debugging.error: IndexError: list index out of range
debugging.why: List me sirf 0 aur 1 index hain; 5 par kuch nahi. Ye SQL + Databases ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Index se pehle length check karo ya safe getter use karo.
debugging.correct:
scores = [10, 20]
print(scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else None)
debugging.lesson: IndexError off-by-one aur empty collection ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye SQL + Databases ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'
debugging.why: int() sirf poore number ka string parse karta hai. Ye SQL + Databases ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

projects.name: SQL + Databases Capstone
projects.problem: Ek believable SQL + Databases use case jo end-to-end chale aur explain ho sake.
projects.objective: LEFT JOIN + COALESCE se un customers ka 0 total bhi aata hai jinke koi order nahi. Isse project interview me trade-offs ke saath present karo.
projects.code:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript('''
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER);
INSERT INTO customers (name) VALUES ('Asha'), ('Ravi');
INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, amount) VALUES (1, 100), (1, 50);
''')
rows = conn.execute('''
SELECT customers.name, COALESCE(SUM(orders.amount), 0) AS total
FROM customers
LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id
GROUP BY customers.id
ORDER BY total DESC
''').fetchall()
print(rows)
projects.explanation: LEFT JOIN + COALESCE se un customers ka 0 total bhi aata hai jinke koi order nahi.
